title: Pangenome-resolved structural variation drives adaptation and trait evolution in cucumber.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Ran paper_context: Europe PMC supplementaryFiles endpoint timed out (one attempt at 120 s), so Supplementary Tables 1-41 were not retrieved. Opened the Zenodo record 10.5281/zenodo.20390974 (CC-BY-4.0): one file, Cucumber.Pangenome-main.zip, 764,778 bytes, which is analysis code only. Listed the GitHub repo xiagjt/Cucumber.Pangenome: markdown pipeline notes, no data tables. NGDC (China National Genomics Data Center) BioProject page PRJCA038097 returns HTTP 200; no file listing inspected.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: 125 long-read assemblies, 202 short-read accessions, 135,597 SVs (structural variants: insertions, deletions, inversions), 38 traits with 172 QTL, an eQTL (expression quantitative trait locus) study in 186 RILs (recombinant inbred lines) with 33,476 SVs and 3,709 lead SVs for 3,207 genes (Supplementary Table 30). The data statement says only assemblies and raw HiFi/Hi-C/RNA-seq reads went to the NGDC GSA archive; no processed SV genotype or expression matrix is named.

a1_downloadable.note: Supplement not retrievable via Europe PMC (timeout); Zenodo and GitHub hold code only (verified). Processed SV genotype and expression matrices are not deposited anywhere stated; only raw reads and assemblies at NGDC GSA (paper text).

a2_label_is_a_column.note: The best label (SV effect on expression) exists only as eQTL summary rows in Supplementary Table 30 per the paper, unseen. Any per-SV expression-effect label beyond that would have to be rebuilt from raw RNA-seq of 186 RILs.

a3_inputs_present.note: SV sequences for a DNA model would have to be extracted from 125 assemblies at NGDC by coordinate; supplementary tables likely carry IDs and coordinates only (not verified).

a5_enough_rows.note: Trait prediction has about 200 accessions (fails). SV-eQTL table could have 3,709 lead SVs (paper text), but unverified.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: unknown; 125 cucumber assemblies (~300 Mb each, ~40 GB) if sequences must be extracted
a6_fits_laptop.note: A subset by coordinate could fit, but needs assembly downloads well over the 50 MB cap.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: No data file opened, so nothing could be compared.

a8_label_provenance.note: eQTL effects derive from measured RNA-seq and genotypes, not from another model; but SV calls themselves are computational.

backbone.name: AgroNT or PlantCaduceus (plant DNA language models) would be the candidates
backbone.hardware: CPU feasible for short windows; not assessed

integration.partner_dataset: Graph-based cucumber pangenome of 39 genomes and 447 accessions (Nature Genetics 2026, s41588-026-02506-0), found by search only
integration.join_key: SV coordinates on the CLv4.0 reference genome (needs coordinate liftover/matching)
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Do SVs predicted to change expression in one cucumber population replicate in an independent pangenome panel?

controls.positive_control: CsFT tandem duplication and INS22773 LTR insertion near CsSPL1, both reported in the paper

honest_claim_h3: At best: predicts which SVs near genes were called significant eQTL in one fruit-tissue RIL cross from two parents, not general SV effects in cucumber.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use the DNA sequence of a large insertion or deletion near a cucumber gene to predict whether it changes that gene's activity.
plain_idea.train_on: Sequence windows around structural variants near genes from 125 cucumber genomes; number of labelled variants unknown (paper says 3,709 lead variants, not verified).
plain_idea.predict: Whether the variant is associated with a change in fruit gene expression, from RNA sequencing of 186 inbred lines from one cross.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Cucumber breeders could prioritise variants for marker development without new expression experiments; failure would show plant DNA models do not capture large-variant effects.

ml_idea: Frozen plant DNA language model embeddings of SV-flanking sequence plus SV length/type/distance-to-TSS features to classify SV-eQTL status; not pursued because label tables and processed matrices were not retrievable.

effort.cheapest_killing_check: Retrieve Supplementary Table 30 from the Nature site or a working supplement endpoint and check whether it lists all tested SVs (negatives) with sequences or just significant lead SVs by ID.

verdict_reason: Only code (Zenodo, 765 KB, verified) and raw reads/assemblies are deposited; supplementary tables were not retrievable, and any label table would hold only significant hits needing sequence extraction from assemblies, with about 200 accessions for trait prediction.
